1.1: [The first person God created was Adam]. Adam’s [son was] Seth. [Seth’s son was] Enosh. [Enosh’s son was] Kenan.
1.2: [Kenan’s son was] Mahalalel. [Mahalalel’s son was] Jared. [Jared’s son was] Enoch.
1.3: [Enoch’s son was] Methuselah. [Methusalah’s son was] Lamech. [Lamech’s son was] Noah.
1.4: [Noah’s sons were] Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
1.5: The sons (OR, descendants) of Japheth were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
1.6: The sons (OR, descendants) of Gomer were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
1.7: The descendants of Javan were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim.
1.8: The sons of Ham were Cush, Mizraim (OR, Egypt), Put, and Canaan.
1.9: The descendants of Cush were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons (OR, descendants) of Raamah were Sheba and Dedan.
1.10: Another descendant of Cush was Nimrod. When he grew up, he became a mighty warrior on the earth.
1.11: Mizraim (OR, Egypt) was the ancestor of the Lud people-group, the Anam people-group, the Lehab people-group, the Naphtuh people-group,
1.12: the Pathrus people-group, the Casluh people-group, and the Caphtor people-group. The people of [the] Philistia [region] were descended from the Casluh people-group.
1.13: Canaan’s first son was Sidon. He was also the ancestor of the Heth people-group,
1.14: the Jebus people-group, the Amor people-group, the Girgash people-group,
1.15: the Hiv people-group, the Ark people-group, the Sin people-group,
1.16: the Arvad people-group, the Zemar people-group, and the Hamath people-group.
1.17: The sons of Shem were Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram. Aram’s sons were Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech.
1.18: Arphaxad was the father of Shelah, who was the father of Eber.
1.19: Eber had two sons. One was named Peleg [which sounds like the word that means ‘divided’] because during the time that he lived, [the people on] the earth were divided [into various language groups]. Peleg’s [younger] brother was Joktan.
1.20: Joktan was the ancestor of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
1.24: The descendants of Shem, [in order from him to Abraham], were Arphaxad, Shelah,
1.27: and Abram, whose [name was later changed to] Abraham.
1.28: Abraham’s sons were Isaac and Ishmael.
1.29: [The son of Abraham’s slave wife Hagar was Ishmael.] Ishmael’s [twelve] sons were Nebaioth, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
1.32: [After ]Abraham’s [wife Sarah died, he took another wife named] Keturah. The sons of Abraham and Keturah were Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. Jokshan’s sons were Sheba and Dedan.
1.33: Midian’s sons were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah.
1.34: The son of Abraham [and his wife Sarah] was Isaac, and Isaac’s sons were Esau and [Jacob, whose name was later changed to] Israel.
1.35: The sons of Esau were Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
1.36: The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho (OR, Zephi), Gatam, Kenaz, Timna, and Amalek.
1.37: Reuel’s sons were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
1.38: [Another descendant of Esau was Seir. His descendants lived in the Edom region]. Seir’s sons were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.
1.39: Lotan’s sons were Hori and Homam, and Lotan’s sister was Timna.
1.40: Shobal’s sons were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam. Zibeon’s sons were Aiah and Anah.
1.41: Anah’s son was Dishon. 1 Dishon’s sons were Hemdan (OR, Hamran), Eshban, Ithran, and Keran.
1.42: Ezer’s sons were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan (OR, Jaakan). Dishan’s sons were Uz and Aran.
1.43: [These are the names of] the kings that ruled [the] Edom [region] before any kings ruled over Israel: Bela, the son of Beor, was king in Edom, and the name of the city [in which he lived] was Dinhabah.
1.44: When Bela died, Jobab, the son of Zerah from Bozrah [city], became the king.
1.45: When Jobab died, Husham became the king. He was from the region where the Teman people-group lived.
1.46: When Husham died, Hadad, the son of Bedad, became the king. He [ruled in] Avith city. Hadad’s [army] defeated [the army of the] Midian [people-group] in [the] Moab [region].
1.47: When Hadad died, Samlah became the king. He was from Masrekah [town].
1.48: When Samlah died, Shaul became the king. He was from Rehoboth [city] along the [Euphrates] river.
1.49: When Shaul died, Baal-Hanan, the son of Achbor, became the king.
1.50: When Baal-Hanan died, Hadad became the king. He was from Pau city. His wife’s name was Mehetabel; she was the daughter of Matred and the granddaughter of Me-Zahab.
1.51: Then Hadad died. The leaders of the clans of the Edom people-group were Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,

2.1: The sons of Jacob were Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,
2.2: Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
2.3: Judah’s sons were Er, Onan, and Shelah. Their mother was the daughter of Shua from the Canaan people-group. [When] Judah’s oldest son Er [grew up, he] did something that Yahweh considered to be very wicked, so Yahweh caused him to die.
2.4: Judah and his daughter-in-law Tamar had [twin boys named] Perez and Zerah. So altogether Judah had five sons.
2.5: The sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.
2.6: Zerah had five sons: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Darda (OR, Dara).
2.7: [One of the sons of Zimri was Carmi]. Carmi’s son Achan (OR, Achar) caused the people of Israel to experience much trouble, because he stole some of the things that had been devoted [to Yahweh to be destroyed].
2.9: Hezron’s sons were Jerahmeel, Ram, and Caleb (OR, Chelubai).
2.10: Ram was the father of Amminadab, and Amminadab was the father of Nahshon. Nahshon was a leader of the tribe of Judah.
2.11: Nahshon was the father of Salmon, who was the father of Boaz.
2.12: Boaz was the father of Obed, and Obed was the father of Jesse.
2.13: Jesse’s oldest son was Eliab. His other sons were Abinadab, Shimea,
2.15: Ozem, and the youngest was David.
2.16: Their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. Zeruiah’s three sons were Abishai, Joab, and Asahel.
2.17: Abigail’s husband was Jether, a descendant of Ishmael, and their son was Amasa.
2.18: Hezron’s younger son Caleb had two wives. One of them, Azubah, gave birth to [three] sons: Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
2.19: When Azubah died, Caleb married Ephrath. Their son was Hur.
2.20: Hur was the father of Uri, and Uri was the father of Bezalel.
2.21: When Hezron was 60 years old, he married Makir’s daughter, who was the sister of Gilead. The son of Hezron and Makir was Segub.
2.22: Segub was the father of Jair. Jair’s [army] controlled twenty-three cities in the region ruled by Gilead.
2.23: But [the armies of] Geshur and Aram captured those towns controlled by Jair. They also captured Kenath [city] and the nearby towns; altogether they captured 60 towns. The people who lived there were all descendants of Makir, the father of Gilead.
2.24: Shortly after Hezron died in Caleb-Ephrath [town], his widow Abijah had a son Asshur; Asshur started Tekoa [town].
2.25: Hezron’s oldest son was Jerahmeel. His sons were Ram, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah. Jerahmeel’s oldest son was Ram.
2.26: Jerahmeel had another wife named Atarah. Their son was Onam.
2.27: The sons of Ram, Jerahmeel’s oldest son, were Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
2.28: Onam’s sons were Shammai and Jada. Shammai’s sons were Nadab and Abishur.
2.29: Abishur’s wife was Abihail. The sons of Abishur and Abihail were Ahban and Molid.
2.30: Nadab’s sons were Seled and Appaim. Seled did not have any children.
2.31: Appaim’s son was Ishi; Ishi’s son was Sheshan. One of Sheshan’s daughters was Ahlai.
2.32: Shammai’s [younger] brother was Jada. Jada’s sons were Jether and Jonathan. Jether did not have any children.
2.33: Jonathan’s sons were Peleth and Zaza. Those were the descendants of Jerahmeel.
2.34: Sheshan did not have any sons; he had only daughters. He had a servant from Egypt whose name was Jarha.
2.35: Sheshan allowed his daughter to marry Jarha, and their son was Attai.
2.36: Attai was the father of Nathan. Nathan was the father of Zabad.
2.37: Zabad was the father of Ephlal. Ephlal was the father of Obed.
2.38: Obed was the father of Jehu. Jehu was the father of Azariah.
2.39: Azariah was the father of Helez. Helez was the father of Eleasah.
2.40: Eleasah was the father of Sismai. Sismai was the father of Shallum.
2.41: Shallum was the father of Jekamiah. And Jekamiah was the father of Elishama.
2.42: Jerahmeel’s [younger] brother was Caleb. Caleb’s oldest son was Mesha. Mesha was the father of Ziph. Ziph was the father of Mareshah. Mareshah was the father of Hebron.
2.43: Hebron’s sons were Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
2.44: Shema was the father of Raham. Raham was the father of Jorkeam. Rekem was the father of Shammai.
2.45: Shammai was the father of Maon. Maon was the father of Beth-Zur.
2.46: Caleb had a slave wife who was named Ephah. Caleb and Ephah’s sons were Haran, Moza, and Gazez. Haran had a son whom he also named Gazez.
2.47: Ephah’s father was Jahdai. Jahdai was the father of [six sons:] Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph.
2.48: Caleb had another slave wife whose name was Maacah. Caleb and Maacah’s sons were Sheber, Tirhanah,
2.49: Shaaph, and Sheva. Shaaph was the father of Madmannah. Sheva was the father of Macbenah and Gibea. Caleb’s daughter was Acsah.
2.50: These people were also descendants of Caleb: [Caleb had another wife whose name was] Ephrathah. Their oldest son was Hur. Hur’s sons were Shobal, Salma, and Hareph. Shobal started Kiriath-Jearim [city]. Salma started Bethlehem [town]. Hareph started Beth-Gader [town].
2.52: Shobal’s descendants were Haroeh, and half of the Manahath people-group.
2.53: His descendants also included these clans that lived in Kiriath-Jearim: Ithri, Put, Shumath, and Mishra. The Zorath and Eshtaol clans were descendants of the Mishra clan.
2.54: Salma’s descendants in Bethlehem were the Netophath clan, the Atroth-Beth-Joab clan, the other half of the Manahath clan, and the Zor clan.
2.55: Salma’s descendants also included the families at Jabez [town] who wrote and copied important documents. These were the Tirath clan, the Shimeath clan, and the Sucath clan. They were all from the Ken people-group who came from Hammath [city], and who had married members of the family of Rechab.

3.1: Six sons of [King] David were born in Hebron [city]. His oldest son was Amnon, whose mother Ahinoam was from Jezreel [city]. His next son was Daniel, whose mother was Abigail from Carmel [city].
3.2: His next son was Absalom, whose mother was Maacah, the daughter of Talmai, the king [who ruled] in Geshur [town]. His next son was Adonijah, whose mother was Haggith.
3.3: The next son was Shephatiah, whose mother was Abital. His youngest son was Ithream, whose mother was Eglah.
3.4: They were all born in Hebron, where David ruled for 7-1/2 years. After that, David ruled in Jerusalem for 33 years.
3.5: Many of David’s children were born in Jerusalem. Bathsheba, the daughter of Ammiel, gave birth to four of his sons: Shammua (OR, Shimea), Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon.
3.6: Nine [other sons of David were also born there. They were] Ibhar, Elishua (OR, Elishama), Eliphelet,
3.9: In addition to all those sons, David’s slave wives also gave birth to sons. David also had one daughter whose name was Tamar.
3.10: Solomon’s son was [King] Rehoboam. Rehoboam’s son was [King] Abijah. Abijah’s son was [King] Asa. Asa’s son was [King] Jehoshaphat.
3.11: Jehoshaphat’s son was [King] Jehoram (OR, Joram). Jehoram’s son was [King] Ahaziah. Ahaziah’s son was [King] Joash.
3.12: Joash’s son was [King] Amaziah. Amaziah’s son was [King] Azariah. Azariah’s son was [King] Jotham.
3.13: Jotham’s son was [King] Ahaz. Ahaz’s son was [King] Hezekiah. Hezekiah’s son was [King] Manasseh.
3.14: Manasseh’s son was [King] Amon. Amon’s son was [King] Josiah.
3.15: Josiah’s oldest son was Johanan. His other sons were Jehoiakim, Zedekiah, and Shallum.
3.16: Jehoiakim’s sons were Jehoiachin (OR, Jeconiah) and Zedekiah.
3.17: [King] Jehoiachin was captured [and taken to Babylon]. His sons were Shealtiel,
3.18: Malkiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
3.19: Pedaiah’s sons were Zerubbabel and Shimei. [Two of] Zerubbabel’s sons were Meshullam and Hananiah, and their sister was Shelomith.
3.20: [Zerubbabel’s] five [other sons were] Hashubah, Ohel, Berekiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab-Hesed.
3.21: The descendants of Hananiah were Pelatiah and Jeshaiah. Jeshaiah’s son was Rephaiah. Rephaiah’s son was Arnan. Arnan’s son was Obadiah. Obadiah’s son was Shecaniah.
3.22: Shecaniah’s son was Shemaiah. Shemaiah’s five sons were Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat.
3.23: Neariah’s three sons were Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam.
3.24: Elioenai’s seven sons were Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani.

4.1: The descendants of Judah were Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
4.2: Shobal’s son was Reaiah. Reaiah was the father of Jahath, and Jahath was the father of Ahumai and Lahad. They were the ancestors of the Zorath people-group.
4.3: The oldest son of Caleb and his wife Ephrathah was Hur. Hur was the one who started/founded Bethlehem [town]. His three sons were Etam, Penuel, and Ezer. Etam’s sons were Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash. Their sister was Hazzelelponi. Penuel was the father of Gedor, and Ezer was the father of Hushah.
4.5: [Hezron’s son] Ashhur, the father of Tekoa, had two wives whose names were Helah and Naarah.
4.6: The sons of Asshur and his wife Naarah were Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari.
4.7: The sons of [Ashhur and his wife] Helah were Zereth, Zohar, Ethnan,
4.8: and Koz. Koz was the father of Anub, Hazzobebah, and the ancestor of the clans descended from Aharhel. Aharhel was the son of Harum.
4.9: [There was another descendant of Judah whose name was] Jabez. [He] was more respected than his brothers were. His mother named him Jabez [which means ‘pain’] because she said, “I was enduring much pain when I gave birth to him.”
4.10: [One day] he prayed to God whom his fellow Israelis [worshiped], saying, “Please greatly bless me and ◄enlarge my land/give me a lot of land/property►. Remain with me, and do not allow anyone to harm me. If you do that for me, I will not have any pain.” And God did what Jabez requested him to do.
4.11: [Another descendant of Judah was] Shuhah. His [younger] brother Kelub was the father of Mehir. Mehir was the father of Eshton.
4.12: Eshton was the father of Beth-Rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah. Tehinnah founded Nahash [town], but their families lived in Recah [town].
4.13: [Another descendant of Judah was] Jephunneh. His son was Caleb. Caleb’s sons were Iru, Elah, and Naam. Elah’s son was Kenaz. The sons of Kenaz were Othniel and Seraiah. Othniel’s sons were Hathath and Meonothai. Meonothai was the father of Ophrah. Seraiah was the father of Joab. Joab was the ancestor of the people who lived in Craftsmen’s Valley. The valley was named that because many of the people who lived there were ◄craftsmen/men who were experts in making things►.
4.16: [Another descendant of Judah was] Jehallelel. His sons were Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel.
4.17: [Another descendant of Judah was Ezrah.] Ezrah’s sons were Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. Mered married Bithiah, who was the daughter of the king of Egypt. The children of Mered and Bithiah were Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah. Ishbah was the father of Eshtemoa. Ezrah also had a wife from Judah. She gave birth to Jered, Heber, and Jekuthiel. Jered was the father of (OR, founded the town of) Gedor, Heber was the father of (OR, founded the town of) Soco, and Jekuthiel was the father of (OR, founded the town of) Zanoah.
4.19: Hodiah’s wife, who was Naham’s sister, bore two sons. One of them was the father of Keilah, the ancestor of the Gar people-group, and the other one was the father of Eshtemoa, the ancestor of the Maacath people-group.
4.20: [Another descendant of Judah was Shimon]. Shimon’s sons were Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-Hanan, and Tilon. [Another descendant of Judah was] Ishi. His descendants were Zoheth and Ben-Zoheth.
4.21: One of Judah’s sons was Shelah. Shelah’s sons were Er the father of Lecah, Laadah the father of Mareshah, the families of those who made things from linen at Beth-Ashbea,
4.22: Jokim, and the men of Cozeba [town], and Joash and Saraph, two men who married women from [the] Moab [region] and later lived in Bethlehem (OR, and ruled in Jashubi-Lehem). All their names and a record of what they did are written in very old scrolls.
4.23: They made pottery for the king; some of them lived in Netaim [town] and some of them lived in Gederah [town].
4.24: Simeon’s sons were Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.
4.25: Shaul’s son was Shallum. Shallum’s son was Mibsam. Mibsam’s son was Mishma.
4.26: Mishma’s son was Hammuel. Hammuel’s son was Zaccur. Zaccur’s son was Shimei.
4.27: Shimei had 16 sons and six daughters, but none of his brothers had many children. So the descendants of Simeon never were as many as the descendants of [his younger brother] Judah.
4.28: The descendants of Simeon lived in [these cities and towns]: Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar-Shual,
4.31: Beth-Marcaboth, Hazar-Susim, Beth-Biri, and Shaaraim. They lived in those places until David became king.
4.32: They also lived in villages near those towns: Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Token, and Ashan.
4.33: There were other villages where they lived, as far [southwest] as Baalath [town]. Those were the places where they lived, and their names, according to the family records.
4.34: The men in the following list were the leaders of their clans: Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah the son of Amaziah, Joel, and Jehu the son of Joshibiah. Joshibiah was the son of Seraiah and the grandson of Asiel. Other clan leaders were Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah, and Ziza. Ziza was the son of Shiphi and the grandson of Allon, who was the son of Jedaiah, who was the son of Shimri, who was the son of Shemaiah. Those families became very large/numerous.
4.39: They went outside of Gedor [town] on the east side of the valley to look for pastureland for their flocks of sheep.
4.40: They found good pastureland with plenty of grass. The place was peaceful and quiet. Previously the descendants of [Noah’s son] Ham had lived there.
4.41: But while Hezekiah was the king of Judah, the leaders of the tribe of Simeon came to Gedor and fought against the descendants of Ham and destroyed their tents. They also fought against the descendants of Meun who were living there, and they killed all of them. So now there are no descendants of Meun living there. The descendants of Simeon started to live there, because there was good pastureland there for their sheep.
4.42: Ishi’s four sons Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah and Uzziel led 500 other descendants of Simeon [and attacked the people who were living] in the hilly area of the Edom [region].
4.43: They killed the few descendants of Amalek who were still alive. From that time until now, the descendants of Simeon have lived in [the] Edom [region].

5.1: Reuben was the oldest son of Jacob. Therefore, he should have received the special rights/privileges that belonged to firstborn sons. But he had sex with his father’s slave wife, so [his father] gave the rights if a firstborn son to the sons of Reubers younger brother Joseph. And in the family records, Reuben is not mentioned first, like the firstborn sons always are.
5.2: Although Judah became more influential than his brothers, and a ruler of the tribe descended from him, Joseph’s family received the rights that belonged to firstborn sons.
5.3: But Reuben was Jacob’s oldest son. Reuben’s sons were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
5.4: [Another descendant of Reuben was Joel]. Joel’s son was Shemaiah. Shemaiah’s son was Gog. Gog’s son was Shimei.
5.5: Shimei’s son was Micah. Micah’s son was Reaiah. Reaiah’s son was Baal.
5.6: Baal’s son was Beerah. Beerah was a leader of the tribe/descendants of Reuben. But Tiglath-Pileser the king of Assyria captured him and took him to Assyria.
5.7: The names of these clans are listed here according to what is written in their family records. The first [name written was] Jeiel. Then Zechariah,
5.8: and then Bela. Bela was the son of Azaz, and Azaz was the son of Shema, and Shema was the son of Joel. Reuben’s clan was very large. Some of them lived near Aroer [city] as far [north] as Nebo [town] and Baal-Meon [city].
5.9: Some of them lived further east, as far as the edge of the desert [south of] the Euphrates River. [They went there] because they had a huge amount of cattle, [with the result that there was not enough pastureland for them] in [the] Gilead [region].
5.10: When Saul was king [of Israel], Bela’s clan fought against the descendants of Hagar and defeated them. After that, Bela’s clan lived in the tents that the descendants of Hagar had lived in previously, in all the area east of [the] Gilead [region].
5.11: The tribe of Gad lived near the tribe of Reuben; they lived in [the] Bashan [region], all the way [east] to Salecah [town].
5.12: Joel was their chief; Shapham was his assistant; other leaders were Janai and Shaphat.
5.13: Other members of the tribe belonged to seven clans, whose leaders were Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber.
5.14: They were descendants of Abihail. Abihail was Huri’s son. Huri was Jaroah’s son. Jaroah was Gilead’s son. Gilead was Michael’s son. Michael was Jeshishai’s son. Jeshishai was Jahdo’s son. Jahdo was the son of Buz.
5.15: Ahi was Abdiel’s son. Abdiel was Guni’s son. Ahi was the leader of their clan.
5.16: The descendants of Gad lived in the towns in Gilead and Bashan regions, and on all the pastureland on [the] Sharon [plain].
5.17: All of those names were written in the records of the clans of Gad during the time that Jotham was the king of Judah and Jeroboam was the king of Israel.
5.18: There were 44,760 soldiers from the tribes of Reuben and Gad and [the eastern] half of the tribe of Manasseh. They all carried shields and swords and bows [and arrows]. They [were all trained to] fight well in battles.
5.19: They attacked the descendants of Hagar and the people of Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab [cities].
5.20: The men from those three tribes prayed to God during the battles, requesting him to help them. So he helped them, because they trusted in him. He enabled them to defeat the descendants of Hagar and all those who were helping them.
5.21: They took the animals that belonged to the descendants of Hagar: They took 50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep, and 2,000 donkeys. They also captured 100,000 people.
5.22: But many descendants of Hagar were killed because God helped the people of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh. After that, those three tribes lived in that area until [the army of] Babylonia [captured them and] took them away to Babylon.
5.23: There were many people who belonged to the eastern half of the tribe of Manasseh. They lived in [the] Bashan [region east of the Jordan River], as far [north] as Baal-Hermon, Senir, and Hermon Mountain.
5.24: Their clan leaders were Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel. They were all strong, brave, and famous soldiers, and leaders of their clans.
5.25: But they sinned against God, the one whom their ancestors had worshiped. They began to worship the gods/idols that the people of that region had worshiped, the people whom God had enabled them to destroy!
5.26: So the God whom the Israelis [worshiped] caused Pul, the king of Assyria, to conquer those tribes. Pul’s other name was Tiglath-Pileser. His [army] captured the people of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the eastern half of the tribe of Manasseh, and took them to [various places in Assyria]: Halah, Habor, Hara and near the Gozan River. [They have lived in those places from that time] to the present time.

6.1: Levi’s sons were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
6.2: Kohath’s sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
6.3: Amram’s children were Miriam and [her younger brothers] Aaron and Moses. Aaron’s sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
6.4: Eleazar was the father of Phinehas. Phinehas was the father of Abishua.
6.5: Abishua was the father of Bukki. Bukki was the father of Uzzi.
6.6: Uzzi was the father of Zerahiah. Zerahiah was the father of Meraioth.
6.7: Meraioth was the father of Amariah. Amariah was the father of Ahitub.
6.8: Ahitub was the father of Zadok. Zadok was the father of Ahimaaz.
6.9: Ahimaaz was the father of Azariah. Azariah was the father of Johanan.
6.10: Johanan was the father of Azariah. Azariah was a priest in the temple that Solomon commanded to be built in Jerusalem.
6.11: Azariah was the father of Amariah. Amariah was the father of Ahitub.
6.12: Ahitub was the father of Zadok. Zadok was the father of Shallum.
6.13: Shallum was the father of Hilkiah. Hilkiah was the father of Azariah.
6.14: Azariah was the father of Seraiah. Seraiah was the father of Jehozadak.
6.15: Jehozadak was forced to leave his home when Yahweh sent [King] Nebuchadnezzar’s [army] to capture many people in Jerusalem and other places in Judah and compel them [to go to Babylonia].
6.16: Levi’s sons were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
6.17: Gershon’s sons were Libni and Shimei.
6.18: Kohath’s sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
6.19: Merari’s sons were Mahli and Mushi. Here is a list of the descendants of Levi, who became leaders of their clans.
6.20: Gershon’s [oldest] son was Libni. Libni’s son was Jehath. Jehath’s son was Zimmah.
6.21: Zimmah’s son was Joah. Joah’s son was Iddo. Iddo’s son was Zerah. Zerah’s son was Jeatherai.
6.22: Kohath’s [other] son was Amminadab. Amminadab’s son was Korah. Korah’s son was Assir.
6.23: Assir’s son was Elkanah. Elkanah’s son was Ebiasaph. Ebiasaph’s son was Assir.
6.24: Assir’s son was Tahath. Tahath’s son was Uriel. Uriel’s son was Uzziah. Uzziah’s son was Shaul.
6.25: Elkanah’s [other] sons were Amasai and Ahimoth.
6.26: Ahimoth’s son was Elkanah. Elkanah’s son was Zophai. Zophai’s son was Nahath.
6.27: Nahath’s son was Eliab. Eliab’s son was Jeroham. Jeroham’s son was Elkanah. Elkanah’s son was Samuel.
6.28: Samuel’s oldest son was Joel; his other son was Abijah.
6.29: Merari’s oldest son was Mahli. Mahli’s son was Libni. Libni’s son was Shimei. Shimei’s son was Uzzah.
6.30: Uzzah’s son was Shimea. Shimea’s son was Haggiah. Haggiah’s son was Asaiah.
6.31: After the Sacred Chest was brought [to Jerusalem, King] David appointed some of the men who were descendants of Levi to be in charge of the music in [the Sacred Tent where the people worshiped] Yahweh.
6.32: Those musicians first sang and played their instruments in the Sacred Tent, which was also called the Tent of Meeting, and they continued to do that until Solomon’s [workers] built the temple of Yahweh in Jerusalem. In all their work, they obeyed the instructions [that David had given them].
6.33: Here is a list of the musicians and their sons: From Kohath’s descendants there was Heman, the leader of the singers. Heman was the son of Joel. Joel was the son of Samuel.
6.34: Samuel was the son of Elkanah. Elkanah was the son of Jeroham. Jeroham was the son of Eliel. Eliel was the son of Toah.
6.35: Toah was the son of Zuph. Zuph was the son of Elkanah. Elkanah was the son of Mahath. Mahath was the son of Amasai.
6.36: Amasai was the son of [another man whose name was] Elkanah. Elkanah was the son of Joel. Joel was the son of Azariah. Azariah was the son of Zephaniah.
6.37: Zephaniah was the son of Tahath. Tahath was the son of Assir. Assir was the son of Ebiasaph. Ebiasaph was the son of Korah.
6.38: Korah was the son of Izhar. Izhar was the son of Kohath. Kohath was the son of Levi. Levi was the son of Jacob.
6.39: Heman’s helper was Asaph. His group [of singers] stood at the right side of Heman. Asaph was the son of Berekiah. Berekiah was the son of Shimea.
6.40: Shimea was the son of Michael. Michael was the son of Baaseiah. Baaseiah was the son of Malkijah.
6.41: Malkijah was the son of Ethni. Ethni was the son of Zerah. Zerah was the son of Adaiah.
6.42: Adaiah was the son of Ethan. Ethan was the son of Zimmah. Zimmah was the son of Shimei.
6.43: Shimei was the son of Jahath. Jahath was the son of Gershon, and Gershon was the son of Levi.
6.44: [A group of singers from] Merari’s family helped Heman and Asaph. They stood to the left of Heman. The leader of this group was Ethan, the son of Kishi. Kishi was the son of Abdi. Abdi was the son of Malluch.
6.45: Malluch was the son of Hashabiah. Hashabiah was the son of Amaziah. Amaziah was the son of Hilkiah.
6.46: Hilkiah was the son of Amzi. Amzi was the son of Bani. Bani was the son of Shemer.
6.47: Shemer was the son of Mahli. Mahli was the son of Mushi. Mushi was the son of Merari, and Merari was the son of Levi.
6.48: The other descendants of Levi were appointed to do other work in the sacred tent, the place [where the people worshiped] Yahweh.
6.49: Aaron and his descendants were the ones who placed on the altar the sacrifices that were to be burned completely, and they burned incense on another altar. Those sacrifices were in order that Yahweh would no longer be angry with the people of Israel for having sinned. Those men also did other work in the Very Holy Place in the sacred tent, obeying the instructions that Moses, who served God [well], had given to them.
6.50: These were the descendants of Aaron: Aaron’s son was Eleazar. Eleazar’s son was Phinehas. Phinehas’s son was Abishua.
6.51: Abishua’s son was Bukki. Bukki’s son was Uzzi. Uzzi’s son was Zerahiah.
6.52: Zerahiah’s son was Meraioth. Meraioth’s son was Amariah. Amariah’s son was Ahitub.
6.53: Ahitub’s son was Zadok, and Zadok’s son was Ahimaaz.
6.54: Here is a list of the places where Aaron’s descendants lived. Those who were descendants of Kohath were the first group to be allotted cities to live in.
6.55: They were allotted Hebron [city] in Judah and the pastureland around the city,
6.56: but the fields farther from the city and the villages near the city were given to Caleb, the son of Jephunneh.
6.57: The descendants of Aaron [who were descendants of Kohath] were allotted Hebron, one of the cities [to which people could flee] and be protected [if they accidentally killed someone]. They also were allotted the towns and pastureland near Libnah, Jattir, Eshtemoa,
6.60: They were also allotted Gibeon, Geba, Alemeth, and Anathoth [cities] from the tribe of Benjamin. Altogether, these clans descended from Kohath were allotted 13 towns.
6.61: The other clans descended from Kohath were allotted ten towns from the clans of the tribe of Manasseh [that lived west of the Jordan River].
6.62: The descendants of Gershon were allotted 13 cities and towns from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and the part of the tribe of Manasseh that lived in [the] Bashan [region on the east side of the Jordan River].
6.63: The descendants of Merari were allotted twelve cities and towns from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
6.64: The leaders of Israel allotted those towns and the nearby pasturelands to the descendants of Levi.
6.65: They also allotted to them the cities and towns from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin that were listed previously.
6.66: Some of the descendants of Kohath were allotted towns from the tribe of Ephraim.
6.67: They were allotted Shechem, which was one of the cities [to which people could flee] and be protected [if they accidentally killed someone], along with the nearby pastureland in the hills of Ephraim. They were also allotted these towns and pastureland near them: Gezer,
6.70: The other descendants of Kohath were allotted Aner and Bileam towns and the nearby pastureland from the part of the tribe of Manasseh that lived west [of the Jordan River].
6.71: The descendants of Gershon, who were part of the tribe of Manasseh, lived east [of the Jordan River]. They were allotted the cities and towns and pastureland near them: Golan in [the] Bashan and Ashtaroth [regions].
6.72: From the tribe of Issachar they were allotted cities and towns and pastureland near Kedesh, Daberath,
6.74: From the tribe of Asher they were allotted cities and towns and pastureland near Mashal, Abdon,
6.76: And from the tribe of Naphtali they were allotted cities and towns and pastureland near Kedesh in [the] Galilee [region], and Hammon and Kiriathaim [towns].
6.77: The other descendants of Levi, those descended from Merari, were allotted towns and pasturelands from the tribe of Zebulun near Jokneam, Kartah, Rimmono, and Tabor.
6.78: From the tribe of Reuben they were allotted cities and towns and pastureland near Bezer in the desert, Jahzah, Kedemoth, and Mephaath. The tribe of Reuben lived east of the Jordan [River], across from Jericho.
6.80: From the tribe of Gad, they were allotted cities and towns and pastureland near Ramoth in [the] Gilead [region], [the cities of] Mahanaim,

7.1: Issachar’s four sons were Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron.
7.2: Tola’s sons were Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Samuel (OR, Shemuel). They were all leaders of the clans [descended from] them. In the record of Tola’s descendants were the names of 22,600 men who served in the army during the time that David was the king [of Israel].
7.3: Uzzi’s son was Izrahiah. Izrahiah’s five sons were Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah. Izrahiah and his sons were all leaders of their clans.
7.4: In the record of Izrahiah’s descendants were the names of 36,000 men who served in the army because they had many wives and children.
7.5: In the records of the clans descended from Issachar were the names of 87,000 men who served in the army.
7.6: [Some of the] sons of Benjamin were Bela, Beker, and Jediael.
7.7: Bela’s five sons were Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri. They were all leaders of clans. In the records of the clans descended from Bela there were names of 22,034 men who served in the army.
7.8: Beker’s sons were Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth.
7.9: In the records of the clans descended from Beker were the names of 20,200 men and leaders of the clans who served in the army.
7.10: Jediael’s son was Bilhan. Bilhan’s sons were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Kenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
7.11: They were all leaders of clans descended from them. There were 17,200 of them who served in the army.
7.12: Shuppim and Huppim were descendants of Ir. [One of] the descendants of Aher was Hushim.
7.13: Naphtali’s sons were Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem. They were all descendants of [Jacob’s slave wife] Bilhah.
7.14: [This is a list of] Manasseh’s descendants. Manasseh had a slave wife who was from Syria. She was the mother of Asriel and Makir. Makir was the father of Gilead.
7.15: Makir [had two wives]. They were from the clans of Huppim and Shuppim. One of Makir’s wives was named Maacah. Another descendant [of Makir] was Zelophehad. Zelophehad [had no sons; he] had only daughters.
7.16: Makir’s wife Maacah gave birth to two sons whom she named Peresh and Sheresh. Sheresh’s sons were Ulam and Rakem.
7.17: Ulam’s son was Bedan. All those [men were considered to be] descendants of Gilead, who was the son of Makir and grandson of Manasseh.
7.18: Makir’s sister name was Hammoleketh who was the mother of Ishdod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
7.19: [One son of Gilead was] Shemida, whose sons were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
7.20: [This is a list of] the descendants of Ephraim. One son of Ephraim’s was Shuthelah. Shuthelah’s son was Bered. Bered’s son was Tahath. Tahath’s son was Eleadah. Eleadah’s son was [also named] Tahath.
7.21: Tahath’s son was Zabad. Zabad’s son was Shuthelah. [Ephraim’s other sons,] Ezer and Elead, went to Gath [city] to steal some cows and sheep. But they were both killed by some of the men from that city.
7.22: Their father Ephraim cried/mourned for them for many days, and his family came to comfort him.
7.23: Then he and his wife had sex [again], and she became pregnant and gave birth to a son. Ephraim named him Beriah [which resembles the word ‘trouble’,] because of the trouble that his family had experienced.
7.24: Ephraim’s daughter was Sheerah. Her workers built [three towns]: Lower Beth-Horon, Upper Beth-Horon, and Uzzen-Sheerah.
7.25: [Another] son of Ephraim was Rephah. Rephah’s son was Resheph. Resheph’s son was Telah. Telah’s son was Tahan.
7.26: Tahan’s son was Ladan. Ladan’s son was Ammihud. Ammihud’s son was Elishama.
7.27: Elishama’s son was Nun. Nun’s son was Joshua, [the man who led the Israelis after Moses died].
7.28: [This is a list of] the cities and areas where the descendants of Ephraim lived: Bethel and the nearby villages; Naaran to the east; Gezer to the west and the nearby villages; and Shechem and the nearby villages. Those villages extended [north] as far as Ayyah and the nearby villages.
7.29: Along the border of the area where the descendants of Manasseh lived were these towns: Beth-Shan, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, and the nearby villages. The people who lived in all those places were descendants of Jacob’s son Joseph.
7.30: Asher’s sons were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah. Their sister was Serah.
7.31: Beriah’s sons were Heber and Malkiel. Malkiel was the father of Birzaith
7.32: Heber was the father of Japhlet, Shomer, and Hotham. Their sister was Shua.
7.33: Japhlet’s sons were Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath.
7.34: Japhlet’s [younger] brother was Shomer. Shomer’s sons were Rohgah, Hubbah, and Aram.
7.35: Shomer’s [younger] brother was Hotham (OR, Helem). Hotham’s sons were Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
7.36: Zophah’s sons were Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,
7.37: Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran [whose other name was Jether], and Beera.
7.38: Jether’s sons were Jephunneh, Pispah, and Ara.
7.39: [Another descendant of Asher was] Ulla, whose sons were Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.
7.40: All those men were descendants of Asher, and they were all leaders of their clans. They were brave warriors and excellent leaders. In the record of the clans that are descended from Asher are [the names of] 26,000 men who served in the army.

8.1: Benjamin had five sons: Bela, Ashbel, Aharah,
8.3: The sons of Bela were Addar, Gera, Abihud,
8.6: [One of Gera’s sons was Ehud.] The descendants of Ehud were leaders of their clans who lived in Geba [city], but they were forced to move to Manahath [city].
8.7: Ehud’s sons/descendants were Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera. Gera was the one who led them when they moved to Manahath. Gera was the father of Uzza and Ahihud.
8.8: [Another descendant of Benjamin was Shaharaim]. He and his wife Hushim had two sons, Abitub and Elpaal. In [the] Moab [region], Shaharaim divorced Hushim and his other wife Baara. [Then he married a woman whose name was] Hodesh, and they had [seven sons]: Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam, Jeuz, Sakia, and Mirmah. They were all leaders of their clans.
8.12: Elpaal’s sons were Eber, Misham, Shemed, Beriah, and Shema. Shemed built [the towns of] Ono and Lod, and the nearby villages. Beriah and Shema were leaders of their clans, who lived in Aijalon [city]. They forced the people who lived in Gath [city] to leave their city.
8.14: Beriah’s sons were Ahio, Shashak, Jeremoth, Zebadiah, Arad, Eder, Michael, Ishpah, and Joha.
8.17: [Other] descendants of Elpaal were Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber,
8.19: [Another descendant of Benjamin was Shimei.] Shimei’s descendants included Jakim, Zicri, Zabdi, Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel, Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath.
8.22: Shashak’s sons were Ishpan, Eber, Eliel,
8.26: [Another descendant of Benjamin was] Jeroham, whose sons were Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah, Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zicri.
8.28: In the records of these clans it is written that all those men were leaders of their clans, and they lived in Jerusalem.
8.29: [Another descendant of Benjamin was] Jeiel. He lived in Gibeon [town], and he was the leader there. His wife was Maacah.
8.30: His oldest son was Abdon. His other sons were Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
8.32: and Mikloth. Mikloth was the father of Shimeah. All these sons of Jeiel also lived near their relatives in Jerusalem.
8.33: Ner was the father of Kish, and Kish was the father of [King] Saul. Saul was the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Esh-Baal.
8.34: Jonathan’s son was Merib-Baal. Merib-Baal was the father of Micah.
8.35: Micah’s sons were Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.
8.36: Ahaz was the father of Jehoaddah. Jehoaddah was the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri was the father of Moza.
8.37: Moza was the father of Binea. The son of Binea was Raphah. The son of Raphah was Eleasah. The son of Eleasah was Azel.
8.38: Azel had six sons: Azrikam, Bokeru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan.
8.39: Azel’s [younger] brother was Eshek. Eshek’s oldest son was Ulam. His other sons were Jeush and Eliphelet.
8.40: Ulam’s sons were brave warriors and ◄good archers/able to shoot arrows well►. Altogether they had 150 sons and grandsons. Those were the descendants of Benjamin.

9.1: The [names of all the] people of Israel were listed/written with the names of their clans, and that information was written in the scroll/book named ‘The Record of the Kings of Israel’. [Many of] the people of Judah were captured and forced to go to Babylon. That happened because they did not faithfully [do what was pleasing to] God.
9.2: The first people who returned [to Judah 70 years later] and lived in their own land and in their own cities and towns were some Israeli priests, other descendants of Levi, and men who worked in the temple.
9.3: [Other] people from the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh [also returned to Judah and] lived in Jerusalem. This is a list of those people [of the tribe of Judah]:
9.4: Uthai the son of Ammihud. Ammihud was the son of Omri; Omri was the son of Imri; Imri was the son of Bani; Bani was a descendant of Perez; Perez was the son of Judah.
9.5: Asaiah and his sons were descendants of Shelah. Asaiah was the oldest son in his family.
9.6: Jeuel and others of his relatives in Zerah’s clan. There were 690 people in this clan.
9.7: From the tribe of Benjamin, Sallu, the son of Meshullam. Meshullam was the son of Hodaviah; Hodaviah was the son of Hassenuah.
9.8: Ibneiah the son of Jeroham. Elah the son of Uzzi. Uzzi was the son of Micri. Meshullam the son of Shephatiah. Shephatiah was the son of Reuel; Reuel was the son of Ibnijah.
9.9: In other records of the people descended from Benjamin, there are the names of 956 people who were living in Jerusalem. All these were leaders of their clans.
9.10: Some of the priests [who returned to Judah were]: Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, Jakin,
9.11: and Azariah who was the son of Hilkiah. Hilkiah who was the son of Meshullam; Meshullam who was the son of Zadok, Zadok who was the son of Meraioth; Meraioth who was the son of Ahitub; Ahitub who supervised the temple guards;
9.12: Adaiah who was the son of Jeroham; Jeroham who was the son of Pashhur; Pashhur who was the son of Malchijah; Maasai who was the son of Adiel; Adiel who was the son of Jahzerah; Jahzerah who was the son of Meshullam; Meshullam who was the son of Meshillemith; Meshillemith who was the son of Immer.
9.13: Altogether there were 1,760 priests [who returned to Judah]. They were leaders of their clans, and they all were responsible for doing work in the temple of God.
9.14: From the descendants of Levi [who returned to Judah] there was Shemaiah the son of Hasshub. Hasshub was the son of Azrikam; Azrikam was the son of Hashabiah; Hashabiah was a descendant of [Levi’s youngest son] Merari.
9.15: [Other descendants of Levi who returned to Judah were] Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah the son of Mica. Mica was the son if Zicri; Zicri was the son of Asaph.
9.16: There was also Obadiah the son of Shemaiah. Shemaiah was the son of Galal. Galal was the son of Jeduthun. There was also Berekiah the son of Asa. Asa was the son of Elkanah, who lived in one of the villages where the Netophath people-clan lived.
9.17: From the [descendants of Levi who returned to Judah] who guarded the temple gates there were Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and some of their relatives. Shallum was their leader.
9.18: Those gatekeepers from the tribe of Levi stood at the King’s Gate on the east side [of the temple].
9.19: Shallum was the son of Kore. Kore was the son of Ebiasaph. Ebiasaph was the son of Korah. Shallum and his relatives were gatekeepers, and they were responsible to guard the gates of the Sacred Tent of Yahweh, like their ancestors had done.
9.20: Previously Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, had supervised the gatekeepers, and Yahweh ◄was with/helped► Phinehas.
9.21: Zechariah the son of Meshelemiah was the gatekeeper at the entrance of the Sacred Tent.
9.22: Altogether, there were 212 men who were chosen to guard the gates. Their names were written in the records of the clans in their villages. [King] David and the prophet Samuel appointed/chose those men because those men ◄were dependable/always did what they were told to do►.
9.23: The work of those gatekeepers and their descendants was to guard the entrances of the Sacred Tent of Yahweh. That was before the temple was built to replace the Sacred Tent.
9.24: There were gatekeepers on each of the four sides of the Sacred Tent.
9.25: Sometimes it was necessary for the relatives of the gatekeepers who lived in those villages to come and help them. Each time some of them came, they helped the gatekeepers for seven days.
9.26: There were four descendants of Levi who [worked every day, and they] supervised the gatekeepers. They also took care of the rooms and treasures in the Sacred Tent of God.
9.27: They remained awake all during the night to guard the Sacred Tent, and each morning they opened the gates.
9.28: Some of the gatekeepers took care of the articles that were used in worship. They also took care of the flour, wine, olive oil, incense, and spices [that were used in the sacrifices].
9.29: Other gatekeepers were appointed to take care of the other things in the Sacred Tent.
9.30: But some of the priests had the work of mixing the spices.
9.31: There was a descendant of Levi named Mattithiah, the oldest son of Shallum, who was a descendant of Korah. He ◄was very dependable/always did what he was told to do►, so they gave him the work of baking the bread that was used in the offerings [on the altar].
9.32: Some of the gatekeepers who were descended from Kohath prepared the freshly baked loaves of sacred bread that were placed on the table [inside the Sacred Tent] every Sabbath/rest day.
9.33: Some of the descendants of Levi were musicians who worked in the Sacred Tent. The leaders of those families [stayed/slept] in the rooms [of the Sacred Tent]. They did not do [any other work] in the Sacred Tent because they were responsible to serve [as musicians] day and night.
9.34: Those are [the names of] the leaders of the clans descended from Levi. Their names were written in the records of the clans. They all lived in Jerusalem.
9.35: [One of the descendants of Benjamin,] Jeiel, lived in Gibeon [city]. He was the city leader. His wife’s name was Maacah.
9.36: His oldest son was Abdon. His other sons were Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
9.38: Mikloth was the father of Shimeam. Jeiel’s family lived near their relatives in Jerusalem.
9.39: Ner was the father of Kish. Kish was the father of [King] Saul. Saul was the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Esh-Baal.
9.40: Jonathan’s son was Merib-Baal. Merib-Baal was the father of Micah.
9.41: Micah’s sons were Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, [and Ahaz].
9.42: Ahaz was the father of Jadah (OR, Jarah). Jadah was the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri was the father of Moza.
9.43: Moza was the father of Binea. The son of Binea was Rephaiah. The son of Rephaiah was Eleasah. The son of Eleasah was Azel.
9.44: Azel had six sons: Azrikam, Bokeru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan.

10.1: The army of Philistia [again] fought against the Israelis. The Israeli soldiers ran away from them, and many Israelis were killed {the soldiers of Philistia killed many Israelis} on Gilboa Mountain.
10.2: The soldiers of Philistia caught up with Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
10.3: The fighting was very fierce around Saul, and the ◄archers/men who shot arrows► shot Saul and wounded him severely.
10.4: Saul said to the man who was carrying his weapons, “Take out your sword and kill me with it, in order that these heathen Philistines will not be able to injure me [further] and make fun of me [while I am dying].” But the man who was carrying Saul’s weapons was terrified and refused to do that. So Saul took his own sword and fell on it [and died].
10.5: When the man carrying his weapons saw that Saul was dead, he also threw himself on his own sword and died.
10.6: So Saul and three of his sons all died, and none of his descendants ever became king.
10.7: When the Israelis who were living in the valley saw that their army had run away and that Saul and his three sons were dead, they left their towns and ran away. Then the soldiers from Philistia came and ◄occupied/lived in► those towns.
10.8: The next day, when the Philistines came to take away the weapons of the dead [Israeli soldiers], they found the corpses of Saul and his three sons on Gilboa Mountain.
10.9: They took the clothes off Saul’s corpse and [cut off] his head and took it and Saul’s armor.
10.10: Then they sent messengers throughout their land, to proclaim the news throughout their own area, to their idols and to the other people. They put Saul’s armor in the temple where their idols were, and they hung Saul’s head in the temple of [their god] Dagon.
10.11: All the people who lived in Jabesh in [the] Gilead [region] heard what the Philistines had done to Saul’s [corpse].
10.12: So the bravest men/soldiers of Jabesh went and got the corpses of Saul and his sons and brought them back to Jabesh. They buried their bones under a large tree in Jabesh. Then the people of Jabesh ◄fasted/abstained from eating food► for seven days.
10.13: Saul died because he did not faithfully obey what Yahweh told him to do. He even went to a woman who talks to the spirits of dead people and asked her what he should do,
10.14: instead of asking Yahweh what he should do. So Yahweh caused him to die, and he appointed David, the son of Jesse, to be the king [of Israel].

11.1: Then the people of Israel came to David at Hebron [town] and said to him, “Listen, we have the same ancestors that you have.
11.2: In the past, when Saul was our king, it was you who led our Israeli [soldiers in our battles]. You are the one to whom Yahweh our God promised, ‘You will be the leader of my people; you will be their king.’”
11.3: So all the Israeli elders came to David at Hebron. And David made a sacred agreement with them while Yahweh was listening. They anointed him [with olive oil to set him apart] to be the king of the Israeli people. That is what Yahweh had previously told [the prophet] Samuel would happen.
11.4: David and all the Israeli [soldiers] went to Jerusalem. [At that time,] Jerusalem was called Jebus, and the people who lived there were the Jebus people-group.
11.5: Those people said to David, “Your [soldiers] will not be able to get inside our city!” But David’s [soldiers] captured the city, even though it had strong walls around it, and since then it has been called ‘The City of David’.
11.6: [What happened was this:]: David said [to his soldiers], “The one who leads [our soldiers] to attack the Jebus people-group will become the commander of all my army.” Joab, the son of Zeruiah, led the soldiers, so he became the commander of all the army.
11.7: [After they captured] the city which had strong walls around it, David moved there. That is why they named it ‘The City of David’.
11.8: David’s workers rebuilt the city, starting where the land was filled in and extending to the wall that was around the city. Joab’s [men] repaired the other parts of the city.
11.9: David became more and more powerful/influential, because the Almighty Commander of the armies of angels was with/helping him.
11.10: Yahweh had promised [that David would become the king]. And all the Israeli people ◄were happy that David was/supported David as► their king. There were many soldiers/warriors who helped David’s kingdom to remain strong.
11.11: This is a list of the leaders of David’s [most mighty] warriors: Jashobeam was from the Hacmon clan. He was one of the leaders of David’s most powerful soldiers. One time he fought against 300 enemies and killed them all with his spear.
11.12: Another one was Eleazar, who was the son of Dodo from the clan of Ahoh.
11.13: [One day] he was with David at Pas Dammim when the soldiers of Philistia gathered there for the battle. There was a field of barley there. At first the Israeli soldiers ran away from the soldiers of Philistia,
11.14: but then David and Eleazar stopped in the middle of the field and fought to defend it and killed [many of] the soldiers of Philistia. Yahweh enabled them to win a great victory on that day.
11.15: One time three of David’s thirty most mighty warriors came to David when he was camping next to the huge rock outside the cave near Adullam. At that same time, the army of Philistia had camped in the Rephaim Valley.
11.16: David was in a fortress, and some of the soldiers of Philistia were occupying Bethlehem.
11.17: [One day] David was very thirsty and said, “I wish that someone would bring me some water from the well near the gate at Bethlehem!”
11.18: So those three most outstanding warriors forced their way through the camp of Philistia soldiers and drew some water from the well, and brought it to David. But he would not drink it. Instead, he poured it out [on the ground to be an offering] to Yahweh.
11.19: He said, “Yahweh, it would certainly not be right for me to drink this water! That would be like drinking the blood of these men who were willing/ready to die for me!” So he refused to drink it. That was one of the things that those three most outstanding warriors did.
11.20: Joab’s [younger] brother Abishai was the leader of the 30 most mighty warriors. [One time] Abishai fought 300 [enemy] soldiers with his spear and killed them.
11.21: So he became as famous as those three most outstanding warriors. He became their commander, even though he was not one of those three men.
11.22: Jehoiada’s son Benaiah was a brave soldier from Kabzeel [town] who did heroic deeds. He killed two of the best warriors from [the] Moab [people-group]. One day he went down into a pit when snow was falling [on the ground] and killed a lion there.
11.23: He also killed a soldier from Egypt who was ◄7-1/2 feet/2.3 meters► tall. The soldier from Egypt carried a spear that was as long as a weaver’s rod. Benaiah had [only] a club, but he grabbed the other man’s spear and killed him with it.
11.24: Those are some of the things that Benaiah did. So he became as famous as the three mighty warriors.
11.25: He was more honored than the other members of the group of thirty most mighty warriors, but he did not become a member of the group of three most outstanding warriors. David appointed him to be the leader of his bodyguards.
11.26: These are the names of David’s mighty warriors: Asahel, the [younger] brother of Joab; Elhanan, the son of Dodo, from Bethlehem;
11.27: Shammah, from [the] Harod [clan]; Helez, from [the] Pelon [clan];
11.28: Ira, the son of Ikkesh, from Tekoa [town]; Abiezer, from Anathoth [city];
11.29: Sibbecai, from Hushah’s [clan]; Ilai from Ahoh’s clan;
11.30: Maharai, from Netophah [town]; Heled, the son of Baanah, also from Netophah [town];
11.31: Ithai, the son of Ribai, from Gibeah [town ] in [the land that belonged to] the tribe of Benjamin; Benaiah, from Pirathon [town];
11.32: Hurai, from the valleys near Gaash [Mountain]; Abiel from the clan of Arabah;
11.33: Azmaveth, from Baharum [town]; Eliahba, from Shaalbon [town];
11.34: The sons of Hashem from [the] Gizon [clan]; Jonathan the son of Shagee from the Harar [town/clan];
11.35: Ahiam the son of Sharar/Sacar, from Harar [town/clan]; Eliphal the son of Ur;
11.36: Hepher from the Mekerath [clan]; Ahijah from the Pelon [clan/town];
11.37: Hezro from Carmel [city]; Naarai the son of Ezbai;
11.38: Joel the [younger] brother of Nathan; Mibhar the son of Hagri;
11.39: Zelek from the Ammon people-group; Naharai, the man who carried Joab’s weapons, from Beeroth [town];
11.41: Uriah, [Bathsheba’s husband], from the Heth people-group; Zabad the son of Ahlai;
11.42: Adina the son of Shiza, a leader from the tribe of Reuben, who had thirty [soldiers] with him;
11.43: Hanan the son of Maacah; Joshaphat from Mithna [town/clan];
11.44: Uzzia from Ashterath [town]; Shama and Jeiel, the sons of Hotham, from Aroer [city];
11.45: Jediael the son of Shimri and his [younger] brother Joha, from Tiz [town/clan];
11.46: Eliel from Mahavah [town/clan]; Jeribai and Joshaviah, the sons of Elnaam; Ithmah from [the] Moab [region];
11.47: Eliel and Obed, and Jaasiel from Zobah [town/clan].

12.1: David went to Ziklag [town] to escape from [King] Saul. While he was there, many warriors came and joined him, and they helped him when he fought battles.
12.2: They carried bows [and arrows]. They were able to shoot arrows and to sling stones. They could use either their right arms or their left arms to do that. They were relatives of Saul from the tribe of Benjamin.
12.3: Their leader was Ahiezer. Next in command was Joash. They were both sons of Shemaah from Gibeah [city]. [These are the names of some of those warriors:] Jeziel and Pelet, the sons of Azmaveth; Beracah; Jehu from Anathoth [town];
12.4: Ishmaiah from the Gibeon [city], who was a leader of the thirty mighty warriors; Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, and Jozabad from Gederah [town];
12.5: Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, and Shephatiah from Haruph [town];
12.6: Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer and Jashobeam, who were descendants of Korah;
12.7: Joelah and Zebadiah, who were sons of Jeroham, from Gedor [town].
12.8: Some men from the tribe of Gad [east of the Jordan River] joined David when he was at his fortress in [the caves in] the desert. They were brave warriors who were trained for fighting battles and able to use shields and spears well. They were as fierce as [SIM, MTY] lions, and they could run as fast as [HYP, SIM] deer/gazelles on the hills/mountains.
12.9: Ezer was their leader. Next in command was Obadiah. Next was Eliab.
12.10: Next was Mishmannah. Next was Jeremiah.
12.11: Next was Attai. Next was Eliel.
12.12: Next was Johanan. Next was Elzabad.
12.13: Next was [another man whose name was] Jeremiah. The last was Macbannai.
12.14: Those men from the tribe of Gad were all army officers. Some of them commanded 1,000 soldiers, and some of them commanded 100 soldiers.
12.15: They crossed [to the west side of] the Jordan [River] during March, [at the time of the year] when the river was flooded. They chased from there all the people who lived in the valleys on both sides of the river.
12.16: Some other men from the tribe of Benjamin and from Judah also came to David in his fortress.
12.17: David went out [of the cave] to meet them and said to them, “If you have come peacefully to help me, I am eager to have you join with me. But if you have come to enable my enemies to capture me, even though I have not done anything to harm you, I hope/wish that the God whom our ancestors ◄worshiped/belonged to► will see it and condemn/punish you.”
12.18: Then [God’s] Spirit came upon Amasai, who was another leader of the thirty [greatest warriors], and he said, “David, we want to be with you; you who are the son of Jesse, we will join you. We know that things will go very well for you and for those who are with you, because your God is helping you.”
12.19: So David welcomed those men, and he appointed them to be leaders of his soldiers. Some men from the tribe of Manasseh also joined David when he went with the soldiers of Philistia to fight against Saul’s [army]. But David and his men did not really help the army of Philistia. After the leaders of Philistia talked [about David and his soldiers], they sent David away. They said, “If David joins his master Saul again, we will all be killed !”
12.20: When David went to Ziklag, these were the men from the tribe of Manasseh who went with him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, [another man whose name was] Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai. Each of them had been a commander of 1,000 men [in Saul’s army].
12.21: They were all brave soldiers, and they helped David to fight against the groups of men who roamed throughout the country, robbing people. So those men became commanders in David’s army.
12.22: Every day more men joined David’s men, and his army became large, like the army of God (OR, a very huge army).
12.23: These are the numbers of soldiers who were ready for battle who joined David at Hebron [city]. They came to help him to become the king of Israel to replace Saul, as Yahweh had promised would happen.
12.24: There were 6,800 men from Judah, who carried shields and spears.
12.25: There were 7,100 men from the tribe of Simeon. They were all strong warriors trained to fight battles.
12.26: There were 4,600 men from the tribe of Levi.
12.27: Jehoiada, who was a leader descended from Aaron, was in that group of descendants of Levi, and there were 3,700 men with him.
12.28: Zadok, a strong young soldier, was also in that group, and there were 22 other leaders from his clan who came with him.
12.29: There were 3,000 men from the tribe of Benjamin who were Saul’s relatives. Most of them had previously wanted one of Saul’s descendants to be the king.
12.30: There were 20,800 men from the tribe of Ephraim who were all brave warriors and trained for fighting battles and famous in their own clans.
12.31: There were 18,000 men from the half of the tribe of Manasseh [that lived west of the Jordan River]. They were all chosen to go and help David become the king.
12.32: There were 200 men who were leaders from the tribe of Issachar, along with their relatives. Those leaders always knew what the Israelis should do, and they knew the right time to do it.
12.33: There were 55,000 men from the tribe of Zebulun. They were all experienced warriors and knew how to use all kinds of weapons well. They were completely loyal to David.
12.34: There were 1,000 officers from the tribe of Naphtali. With them were 37,000 soldiers, each carrying shields and spears.
12.35: There were 28,600 soldiers from the tribe of Dan, all trained to fight battles.
12.36: There were 47,000 experienced soldiers from the tribe of Asher, all trained to fight battles.
12.37: There were also 120,000 soldiers from the area east of the Jordan [River who joined David]. They were from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the eastern half of the tribe of Manasseh. They had all kinds of weapons.
12.38: All those men were soldiers who volunteered to be in David’s army. They came to Hebron wanting very much to enable David to be the king of all of the Israeli people.
12.39: The men spent three days there with David, eating and drinking, because their families had given them food to take with them.
12.40: Also, their fellow Israelis came from as far away as the area where the tribes of Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali lived, bringing food on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen. They brought a lot of flour, fig cakes, raisins, wine, [olive] oil, cattle and sheep. And throughout Israel, the people were very joyful.

13.1: [One day] David talked with all his army officers. Some of them were commanders of 100 soldiers and some were commanders of 1,000 soldiers.
13.2: Then he summoned the other Israeli leaders and said to all of them, “If it seems to you to be a good thing for us to do, and if it is what Yahweh our God wants, let’s send a message to our fellow Israelis in all the areas of our country, including the priests and [other] descendants of Levi who are living among them in their towns and in the nearby pasturelands, to come and join us,
13.3: because we want to bring the Sacred Chest of our God back to us. While Saul [was the king], we did not go to God’s presence to ask him what we should do.”
13.4: All the people agreed with David, because they all thought that it was the right thing to do.
13.5: So David gathered all the Israeli people, from the Shihor [River ] in Egypt to Lebo-Hamath [town in the north, and told them that he wanted them] to [help] bring the Sacred Chest of God [back to Jerusalem] from Kiriath-Jearim [city].
13.6: David went with all the Israeli people to Baalah [town], which is [another name for] Kiriath-Jearim, to get the Sacred Chest. [The people believed that] God ruled from between the statues of winged creatures that was above the lid of the Sacred Chest .
13.7: The people put the Sacred Chest on a new cart and transported it from Abinadab’s house. Uzzah and Ahio were guiding [the oxen that were pulling the cart].
13.8: David and all the Israeli people were celebrating in God’s presence with all their strength. They were singing and [playing] lyres, harps, tambourines, and cymbals, and [blowing] trumpets.
13.9: But when David’s men came to the place where Kidon threshed grain, the oxen stumbled. So Uzzah reached out with his hand to prevent the Sacred Chest from falling off the cart.
13.10: Yahweh immediately became very angry with Uzzah, and he caused Uzzah to suddenly die there because he had put his hand on the Sacred Chest, [and Yahweh had commanded that only the descendants of Levi who help the priests should touch the Sacred Chest].
13.11: David was angry because Yahweh had punished Uzzah. And now that place [where Uzzah died] is called ‘The Punishment of Uzzah’.
13.12: That day, David was afraid of God. He asked [himself], “◄How can I bring God’s Sacred Chest to my [city]?/I am afraid to bring God’s Sacred Chest to my [city].►”
13.13: So the men with David did not take the Sacred Chest to Jerusalem. Instead, they took it to the house of Obed-Edom, who was from Gath [city].
13.14: The Sacred Chest stayed with Obed-Edom’s family in his house for three months. And [during that time] Yahweh blessed Obed-Edom’s family and everything that he owned.

14.1: One day Hiram, the king of Tyre [city], sent some messengers to David [to talk about making an agreement between their countries]. Then Hiram sent cedar logs, bricklayers, and carpenters to build a palace for David.
14.2: [When that happened,] David knew that Yahweh had truly caused him to be the king of Israel, and that he had caused his kingdom to be greatly respected. Yahweh did this because [he loved] his Israeli people.
14.3: David married more women in Jerusalem, and [those women] gave birth to more sons and daughters for him.
14.4: The names of the children that were born to him there in Jerusalem are Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
14.8: When the army of Philistia heard that David has been appointed to be king of all of Israel, they came to capture him. But David heard that they were coming, so he [and his soldiers] marched out to fight against them.
14.9: The army of Philistia had attacked the people in the Rephaim Valley [southwest of Jerusalem] and had robbed them.
14.10: David asked God, “Should [my men and] I go and attack the army of Philistia? [If we go,] will you enable us to defeat them?” Yahweh replied, “Yes, go, and I will enable you to defeat them.”
14.11: So David and his men went up to a town where the soldiers of Philistia were staying and defeated them. Then David said, “God has enabled me [and my soldiers] to overwhelm my enemies like a flood.” So they named that place ‘Baal-Perazim’ [which means ‘Yahweh breaks through’].
14.12: [As the soldiers of Philistia fled], they left their idols there. So David commanded his soldiers to burn those idols.
14.13: But soon the army of Philistia attacked the people in that valley again.
14.14: So again David prayed to God [to ask him what he should do], and God replied, saying “Do not attack the army of Philistia from the front. Instead, go around them, and attack them [from the rear] in front of the balsam trees.
14.15: When you hear something in the tops of the balsam trees that sounds like [soldiers] marching, attack them. I, God, will have gone ahead of you to enable you to defeat the army of Philistia.”
14.16: So David did what God commanded him to do, and he and his army defeated the army of Philistia, all the way from Gibeon [city in the east] to Gezer [city in the west].
14.17: So David became famous in all the nearby countries, and Yahweh caused [the leaders of] all the [nearby] nations to be afraid of him.

15.1: David [commanded his workers to] build some houses for him in Jerusalem. He also told them to set up a tent in which to put the Sacred Chest.
15.2: He said, “Only the descendants of Levi are permitted to carry God’s Sacred Chest, because they are the ones whom God chose to carry it and to serve him forever.”
15.3: David summoned all the people of Israel to come to Jerusalem. He wanted the Sacred Chest of Yahweh to be put in the place that he had made for it.
15.4: He summoned the descendants of Aaron, [who was the first Supreme Priest,] and the other descendants of Levi.
15.5: 120 descendants of Kohath, who was Levi’s second son, came, with Uriel their leader.
15.6: There were 220 descendants of Merari, Levi’s third son, who came, with Asaiah their leader.
15.7: There were 130 descendants of Gershon, Levi’s first son, who came, with Joel their leader.
15.8: There were 200 people from Elizaphan’s clan who came, with Shemaiah their leader.
15.9: There were 80 people from Hebron’s clan who came, with Eliel their leader.
15.10: And there were 112 people from Uzziel’s clan who came, with Amminadab their leader.
15.11: David summoned the priests Zadok and Abiathar and these [other] descendants of Levi: Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab.
15.12: David said to them, “You are the leaders of the clans descended from Levi. You and the other descendants of Levi must purify yourselves, in order to [be able to do this special work for Yahweh. You must] bring the Sacred Chest of Yahweh, the God of us Israelis, up to the place that I have made for it [here in Jerusalem].
15.13: The first time that we tried to bring it, we did not ask Yahweh how we should carry it . You [descendants of Levi] were not the ones who carried it, so Yahweh our God punished us.”
15.14: Then the priests and the [other] descendants of Levi [performed the rituals to] purify themselves, in order that it would be proper for them to do the work of carrying the Sacred Chest of Yahweh, the God of us Israeli people.
15.15: The descendants of Levi [inserted] the poles [into the rings on] the Sacred Chest so that with them, they could carry the Sacred Chest on their shoulders, like Moses had commanded, and like Yahweh had said that they should.
15.16: David told the leaders of the descendants of Levi to appoint some of their relatives to sing joyful songs and play lyres, harps, and cymbals [while they were carrying the Sacred Chest].
15.17: So they appointed Heman and his relatives Asaph and Ethan. Heman was the son of Joel; Asaph was the son of Berekiah. Ethan, a descendant of Merari, was Kushaiah’s son.
15.18: There was also another group of descendants of Levi who were appointed: Zechariah, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, and two of the Sacred Tent gatekeepers, Obed-Edom and Jeiel.
15.19: Heman, Asaph and Ethan sang, and also played bronze cymbals.
15.20: Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah played lyres.
15.21: Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, Jeiel and Azaziah played harps.
15.22: Kenaniah, the leader of the descendants of Levi, directed the singing because he was very skilled at doing that.
15.23: Berekiah and Elkanah were two of the men who guarded the Sacred Chest.
15.24: The priests Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer were appointed to blow trumpets in front of the Sacred Chest. Obed-Edom and Jehiah also guarded the Sacred Chest.
15.25: David and the Israeli leaders and the officers who commanded 1,000 soldiers went to bring the Sacred Chest back from Obed-Edom’s house. They were very joyful as they brought it to Jerusalem.
15.26: God helped the descendants of Levi who carried the Sacred Chest of Yahweh; therefore David and the leaders sacrificed seven bulls and seven ◄rams/male sheep► [to thank him].
15.27: All the descendants of Levi who carried the Sacred Chest, all the singers, and Kenaniah, the man who directed those who sang, wore robes of fine white linen and sacred vests made of fine linen. David also wore a sacred vest made of white linen.
15.28: So all of the Israeli people joined in bringing the Sacred Chest up [to Jerusalem]. They shouted [joyfully, while the musicians] blew horns and trumpets, and played cymbals, lyres, and harps.
15.29: While they were bringing the Sacred Chest into Jerusalem, Saul’s daughter Michal watched them, looking out of a window. When she saw King David dancing and celebrating, she despised him.

16.1: They brought the Sacred Chest [to Gibeon] and put it inside the Sacred Tent that David had [told his workers to] set up. Then they brought offerings to be completely burned [on the altar] and offerings to enable them to maintain fellowship [with God].
16.2: When David had finished presenting all those offerings, he [asked Yahweh to] bless the people.
16.3: He gave a loaf of bread, some dates, and some raisins to every Israeli man and woman [who was there].
16.4: Then David appointed some of the descendants of Levi to stand in front of [the Sacred Tent in which] the Sacred Chest [had been placed], to lead the people who worshiped and thanked and praised Yahweh, the God of the Israeli people.
16.5: Asaph, who played the cymbals, was their leader. Zechariah was his assistant. The other descendants of Levi [who helped Asaph] were Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel. They played lyres and harps.
16.6: Benaiah and Jahaziel were priests who blew trumpets frequently in front of [the Sacred Tent in which was] the Sacred Chest.
16.7: On that day, David gave to Asaph and his helpers this psalm to praise Yahweh:
16.8: Thank God, and pray to him . Tell the people of all nations what he has done.
16.9: Sing to him; sing songs to praise him. Tell about all his miraculous deeds.
16.10: Be glad that you belong to him ; those who want to know Yahweh better should rejoice.
16.11: Trust in Yahweh and in his power; continually seek to get help from him.
16.12: Do not forget the wonderful things that he has done, the miracles and the just laws that he has given to us.
16.13: We people are the descendants of his servant Jacob; we are the people of Israel whom he has chosen.
16.14: Yahweh is our God. His just/fair laws are known by people throughout the world.
16.15: He never forgets the agreement that he has made: he made a promise that will last for 1,000 generations.
16.16: That is the agreement that he made with Abraham, and he repeated that agreement to Isaac.
16.17: It was an agreement for the Israeli people, and he wanted that agreement to endure forever.
16.18: What he said was, “I will give the Canaan region to you, to belong to you [and your descendants forever].”
16.19: [He said that to them] when there were only a few of them, a tiny group of people who were living in that land ◄like strangers/that belonged to other people►;
16.20: they continued to wander from one place to another, from one kingdom to another.
16.21: But he did not allow others to oppress them, and he warned kings by saying to them,
16.22: “Do not harm the people whom I have chosen! Do not harm my prophets!”
16.23: You people throughout the world, sing to Yahweh. Every day proclaim [to others] that he has saved us.
16.24: Tell the people of the nations that he is great; tell all the people-groups the marvelous things [that he has done].
16.25: Yahweh is great, and he deserves to be praised very much. He should be revered more than all the gods,
16.26: because all the gods that the [other] people-groups [worship] are only idols, but Yahweh [is truly great; he] created the skies.
16.27: He is glorious and majestic; his power and joy fill his Sacred Tent.
16.28: You people in nations all over the world, praise Yahweh! Praise Yahweh for his glorious power [HEN]!
16.29: Praise Yahweh like he deserves to be praised. Bring an offering and come to his Sacred Tent. Worship Yahweh because he is holy.
16.30: Everyone on the earth should tremble in front of Yahweh. He put the earth firmly [in its place]; and nothing ever will be able to move/shake it.
16.31: Everything in the sky and on the earth should be happy. People [everywhere] should say, “Yahweh is our king!”
16.32: The oceans and all the creatures that are in the oceans should shout to praise him; the fields and everything that is in them should rejoice.
16.33: When they do that, [it will be as though] the trees in the forest will sing joyfully in front of Yahweh. That will happen when he comes to judge [everyone on] the earth.
16.34: Thank Yahweh, because [everything that he does is ] good. He faithfully loves us forever.
16.35: Say to him, “God, you are the one who rescues us, so gather us together and save us from [the armies of] other nations. When you do that, we will thank you , and we will be happy to praise you.”
16.36: Praise Yahweh, the God of us Israeli people, He has always existed, and he will exist forever. After the people [finished singing that song], they all said, “◄Amen/May it be so►!”, and they praised Yahweh.
16.37: Then David left Asaph and the other members of his clan there in front of [the tent in which] Yahweh’s Sacred Chest [had been placed]. He told them that they must do their work there every day.
16.38: David also left Obed-Edom and 68 other descendants of Levi to work with them. Hosah and Obed-Edom guarded [the entrances of the Sacred Tent].
16.39: David also told Zadok the [Supreme] Priest and the other priests who worked with him to remain in front of Yahweh’s Sacred Tent, which was still at the place where the Israeli people worshiped [God there] in Gibeon [city].
16.40: Every morning and every evening they burned offerings on the altar, obeying the rules/laws that had been written [by Moses], rules/laws which Yahweh had given to the Israeli people.
16.41: With them were Heman and Jeduthun and other descendants of Levi. They were chosen to sing songs to praise Yahweh because he faithfully loves his people forever.
16.42: Heman and Jeduthun were appointed to play the trumpets and cymbals when [the other descendants of Levi sang sacred songs]. The sons of Jeduthun were appointed to guard the gates [of the Sacred Tent].
16.43: Then all the people left. They returned to their homes, and David returned home to [ask Yahweh to] bless his family.

17.1: After David began to live in his palace, he said to the prophet Nathan, “[It does not seem right that] I am here living in a palace made of cedar [wood], but Yahweh’s Sacred Chest is kept inside a tent!”
17.2: Nathan replied to David, “Whatever you are thinking about doing, do it, because God is with/guiding you.”
17.3: But that night God spoke to Nathan. He said,
17.4: “Go and tell my servant David that this is what I, Yahweh, am saying to him: ‘You are not the one who should build a temple for me to live in.
17.5: I have not lived in any building, from the day that I brought the people of Israel up [out of Egypt] until now. Instead, I have [lived in a tent], moving from one place to another with [the Israelis] when they moved to other places .
